text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: control-plane error-rate spike — elevated 5xx across API gateway. Paging #oncall (ryan_oncall). Please ack and triage. link: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/CP-errors

marta: acked. seeing 502/504s from control-plane auth + org-lookup paths, started ~5m ago. spikes align with increased org-lookup latency P95.

ryan_oncall: on it. grabbing traces and correlating with deploys. @eng_runtime any recent infra churn?

eng_runtime: no infra deploys in last 30m. we have a config push 12m ago to config-service, but rollout flagged as partial.

sre_jules: logs look like auth-service upstream returning 503s intermittently, and billing-service shows request throttles -> 429 -> downstream turned into 502s by gateway.

marta: quick customer impact: API requests to /v1/auth and /v1/org/* are failing for ~12% of requests globally, higher in eu-west-1. Some customers report UI errors.

ryan_oncall: running quick queries: 
```
# kql-ish
sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=\"gateway\",status=~\"5..\",route=~\"/v1/(auth|org).*\"}[1m])) by (region)
```
results: eu-west spikes to 60rps 5xx, us-east ~8rps.

eng_runtime: adding a temporary request-rate cap and increasing alpha circuit-breaker window for auth upstream to avoid cascades. Pushing rule now.

bot-deploy: deploy started: firewall-rule-update-2026-03-15 (id: dr-9921)

marta: hold on deploy. if config push is related we should pause until we confirm. Can we rollback that config?

eng_runtime: pausing deploy. rollback available: `config-service: rollback v2.14 -> v2.13` but need owner signoff. It touched org-lookup caching TTL.

ryan_oncall: can we patch a defensive change in gateway to treat upstream 429 from billing as 429 instead of 502? That would reduce false 5xx surface.

sre_jules: yes, we can apply a temporary transform rule at gateway (edge-rule) to map billing 429->429 and short-circuit 5xx inflation. Applying now.

eng_runtime: applied edge-rule: `map-upstream-status(billing,429)->429` across edge nodes in eu-west and us-east. Confirming propagation.

marta: metrics showing 5xx rate dropping in eu-west from 60rps -> 22rps after rule, still elevated.

product_lead: any customer-visible mitigation we can suggest? status page note?

ryan_oncall: create incident page update: short note that partial auth/org errors observed, mitigation in progress. I'll post a brief update in 10m.

eng_runtime: investigating config-service rollout: the TTL decrease meant more cache misses for org-lookup -> dramatic spike in downstream auth calls. That amplified billing quota checks -> throttling. If we rollback TTL to previous value, it should reduce backend load.

marta: agree. let's rollback the config-service TTL change. Who can execute?

eng_runtime: I'll trigger rollback. Executing: `kubectl set image config-service config=v2.13` then `kubectl annotate rollout/confirm=true`.

bot-deploy: rollback initiated (id: rb-3344). Expected completion ~45s.

sre_jules: while rollback happens, increase auth-service replica count in eu-west from 3->6 to absorb extra requests short term.

eng_runtime: scaling auth-service replicas now. `kubectl scale deploy/auth-service --replicas=6 -n prod-eu-west`

marta: auth latency P95 improving slightly but billing throttle still present. Billing team pinged for quota bump or temporary relax. @product_lead FYI.

product_lead: pinged billing ops. they can raise soft limits for 20 minutes while we stabilize.

ryan_oncall: good. after rollback and gateway mapping, 5xxs dropped to ~6% globally and eu-west to ~4%. Customer reports decreasing.

eng_runtime: rollback finished. config-service back to v2.13. Cache warmup in progress — expecting full relief in 5-10m as caches repopulate.

sre_jules: adding a short-lived cache-warm job to prepopulate org entries for high-volume accounts: `python prewarm_org_cache.py --top-n 200` running now.

marta: running synthetic checks: run /v1/org/lookup for sample accounts — success rate improving from 78% -> 95% within 3m.

bot-deploy: deploy/rollback rb-3344 succeeded.

ryan_oncall: status update for incident page: "Mitigations applied: edge mapping for billing 429s, config-service rollback restoring cache TTL, auth-service scaled. Error rates reduced. Investigating root cause and postmortem to follow." Will publish now.

product_lead: customers to notify: top-20 affected accounts, support is drafting messages. No major financial impact expected, but UX degraded for some.

eng_runtime: retention: we'll revert temporary gateway mapping after billing quota normalizes. Also propose a safe rollout checklist for config-service changes that affect TTLs + prewarm job.

marta: oncall handoff: ryan_oncall to jules in 30m. ryan staying for the handoff.

ryan_oncall: ack. I'll prepare a short runbook note: steps taken, commands, and links to dashboards.

sre_jules: thanks. I'll monitor for the next 60m and start working on RCA once we verify stable baseline.

marta: summary: root cause chain: config TTL change -> increased org-lookup miss rate -> amplified auth calls -> billing throttle -> gateway 5xx inflation. Mitigations: rollback TTL, map billing 429->429 at gateway, scale auth-service, cache prewarm, billing soft-limits. Next: RCA, test rollout gating, and postmortem.

bot-deploy: incident closed to pager (status: mitigated). If errors rise above threshold reopen.

ryan_oncall: final note: we've collected traces and span IDs for affected windows, saved to /incidents/2050000000/artifacts. Assigning RCA owners: eng_runtime (config-service) + sre_jules (oncall ops).

marta: thanks team. tagging for postmortem: #postmortems and scheduling 1hr RCA sesh tomorrow.

sre_jules: leaving monitoring watch; will escalate if any resurrection. :thumbsup:

marta: closing thread in 10m unless new alerts.
